name: honesty
description: Perception that someone's words or actions reflect an effort do the 'right' thing rather than a more self-beneficial thing.

variations.name: witnessing honesty
variations.description: If someone said or did something 'right' that doesn't obviously benefit them, you may feel admiration, anger, sympathy, contempt, or a mix. It depends on who it was, what they said, and how it affects you.

variations.name: uncomfortable honesty
variations.description: Someone said something truthful that creates a feeling of sympathetic cringey embarassment.

variations.name: honest work
variations.description: Working hard at something that helps some without unduly harming others.

variations.name: unrecognized honesty
variations.description: Sense of disappointment that you're being honest with someone by they don't believe you.

variations.name: self honesty
variations.description: Allowing different internal impulses attention and time to recognize each other and work things out.

commentaries.quote: How desperately difficult it is to be honest with oneself. It is much easier to be honest with other people.
True honesty is difficult because words always only tell part of a complex story and then echo through time. Sometimes not saying something is the most nuanced form of honesty.

We appreciate honesty because trust makes our decisions about a person less doubtful, and doubt is pain. But there are some that may take advantage of information, so the wise will strive to speak honestly but only speak when necessary.
